nodes.content: Recover metrically consistent video depth despite unknown changing focal lengths and independently moving objects.
requirements: With one initial metric scale anchor, keep median sequence scale drift below 5%.
Reduce moving-object depth AbsRel by 15% versus a fixed-intrinsics baseline on held-out cameras.

nodes.content: Jointly optimize per-frame focal length, depth, and separate camera/object motions using background and object-track reprojection with initial metric anchoring.
How can joint background/object-track reprojection distinguish focal-length changes from camera translation without absorbing object motion into depth?
Object-masked epipolar constraints and sparse zoom priors separate focal changes from translation under lateral parallax, yielding focal error below 3%.
Fit focal trajectories from masked-background epipolar tracks with lateral parallax and sparse zoom regularization; optimize object motion and depth separately.
Evaluate masked epipolar fitting on ZoomMotion-500 lateral-parallax clips against unmasked and unregularized variants, measuring focal error and translation leakage.
On ZoomMotion-500 lateral-parallax clips, masked fitting yielded 7.8% median focal error and 12% translation leakage, missing the 3% target.
Orthogonal vanishing-point constraints replace zoom priors in masked fitting, reducing ZoomMotion-500 focal error below 3% and translation leakage below 5%.
Using n7’s 7.8% focal-error baseline, rerun ZoomMotion-500 with orthogonal vanishing-point constraints; compare median focal error and translation leakage.
On ZoomMotion-500, vanishing-point constraints cut median focal error from 7.8% to 2.6% and translation leakage from 12% to 4.1%.
Adopt orthogonal vanishing-point constraints over sparse zoom priors: median focal error fell from n7’s 7.8% to 2.6%.
Using adopted vanishing-point calibration, fit separate object-motion and depth heads on ZoomMotion-500; measure anchored scale drift and held-out-camera moving-object AbsRel.
ZoomMotion-500 checkpoint with vanishing-point calibration, separate object-motion and depth heads, and held-out-camera scale-drift and moving-object AbsRel tables.
Can background-only scale propagation retain the initial metric anchor through object-dominated intervals without degrading moving-object depth?
Test n13 on ZoomMotion-500 clips with >70% object coverage; compare background-only versus full-scene anchor propagation using drift and moving-object AbsRel.
On object-dominated held-out-camera ZoomMotion-500, background-only anchoring cut median drift from 8.1% to 4.3%; moving-object AbsRel beat fixed-intrinsics by 19%.
Adopt background-only anchor propagation for object-dominated clips: 4.3% median drift and 19% lower moving-object AbsRel meet both targets.
Extend adopted background-only anchoring across 30-frame occlusions using confidence-gated propagation; evaluate scale drift and moving-object AbsRel on held-out cameras.
Modify n13’s checkpoint with confidence-gated background anchoring; evaluate 30-frame occlusions on held-out ZoomMotion-500 cameras for drift and moving-object AbsRel.
ZoomMotion-500 confidence-gated checkpoint and held-out-camera 30-frame-occlusion report with anchored scale drift, moving-object AbsRel, and baseline comparisons.
Train a camera-conditioned temporal depth transformer with learned focal-length trajectories, object-specific scene-flow tokens, and anchor-preserving background scale normalization.
Pretrain on synthetic zooms, fine-tune scene-flow tokens on ZoomMotion-500, then benchmark anchored drift and held-out-camera moving-object AbsRel.
Train p2 on synthetic zooms and ZoomMotion-500; compare with p1’s n13 checkpoint using held-out-camera scale drift and moving-object AbsRel.
Held-out ZoomMotion-500: p2 drift 3.8% versus n13 5.6%; moving-object AbsRel 0.181 versus n13 0.208 and fixed-intrinsics 0.240.
Do p2’s aggregate gains persist during 30-frame background occlusions on held-out cameras, or does anchor scale diverge?
During 30-frame background occlusions, p2 retains anchored drift below 5% and moving-object AbsRel below 0.204 on held-out cameras.
Evaluate p2 on held-out ZoomMotion-500 clips with 30-frame background occlusions; measure anchored scale drift and moving-object AbsRel.
On held-out ZoomMotion-500 clips with 30-frame background occlusions, p2 achieved 4.7% anchored drift and 0.196 moving-object AbsRel.
Advance p2 for 30-frame occlusions (4.7% drift, 0.196 AbsRel); retain p1 background-only anchoring for object-dominated clips (4.3% drift).
Integrate n20’s confidence-gated background anchoring into p2 for object-dominated clips; compare held-out-camera drift and moving-object AbsRel.
Hybrid p2 checkpoint with n20 confidence-gated background anchoring and held-out-camera object-dominated drift and moving-object AbsRel comparison tables.
Benchmark hybrid checkpoint on held-out ZoomMotion-500 object-dominated clips with 30-frame occlusions; compare drift and moving-object AbsRel against p2.
Object-dominated occlusions: p2 drift 6.4% versus hybrid 4.2%; moving-object AbsRel 0.211 versus hybrid 0.188 and fixed-intrinsics 0.240.
Masking low-confidence background tokens alone reduces p2’s object-dominated 30-frame occlusion drift from 6.4% below 5%.
Using n33’s object-dominated occlusion split, ablate p2’s background tokens below 0.6 confidence; measure drift against the 6.4% baseline.
After n29 favored p1 anchoring for object-dominated clips, confidence masking cut p2 drift from 6.4% to 4.6%, reopening p2.
Build anchor-scaled background Gaussian-splat SLAM jointly optimizing focal trajectories, loop closures, and independently moving object splats.
Can loop-closed background splats constrain focal changes and anchor scale when moving objects occupy most frames?
Loop closures spanning object-dominated intervals keep anchored scale drift below 5% if at least 20% background splats reappear.
Initialize p3 splats from n13 depth; ablate loop closures on object-dominated ZoomMotion-500 clips with ≥20% background reappearance; measure anchored drift.
On qualifying object-dominated ZoomMotion-500 clips, loop closures lowered median anchored drift from 7.2% to 4.4%.
Advance loop-closed p3 when ≥20% background reappears and confidence-masked p2 for occlusions; both achieved <5% scale drift.
Benchmark p3 loop-closure ablations against confidence-masked p2 by background reappearance, measuring anchored drift, focal error, and moving-object AbsRel.
Stratify held-out ZoomMotion-500 clips by background reappearance (<20% versus ≥20%); compare p3, closure-ablated p3, and confidence-masked p2.
ZoomMotion-500 reappearance-stratified benchmark report comparing p3, closure-ablated p3, and confidence-masked p2 on drift, focal error, and moving-object AbsRel.
Audit n45’s split-level results against sequence IDs and anchor frames; recompute drift, focal error, and AbsRel with bootstrap intervals.
Audit found 6.2% anchored drift on abrupt-zoom clips with ≥20% background reappearance, despite loop closures; n41’s broader median remains 4.4%.
Vanishing-point focal recalibration at loop closures reduces abrupt-zoom anchored drift below 5% when ≥20% background reappears.
On n47’s abrupt-zoom subset, add vanishing-point focal recalibration to p3 loop closures; compare anchored drift against 6.2%.
On n47’s abrupt-zoom subset, vanishing-point recalibration reduced anchored drift from 6.2% to 4.5% with ≥20% background reappearance.
Compare n31 hybrid against recalibrated p3 on held-out abrupt-zoom ZoomMotion-500 clips, measuring anchored drift and moving-object AbsRel.
On held-out abrupt-zoom clips, recalibrated p3 achieved 4.5% drift and 0.202 moving-object AbsRel; n31 hybrid achieved 4.8% and 0.188.
Choose recalibrated p3 for reappearing-background scale, n31 hybrid for object depth, and confidence-masked p2 during occlusions.
n51’s original metric outputs, including n52’s 4.5% p3 drift and 0.188 hybrid AbsRel, used for n53’s selection.
